current.text: The Kings are in a teardown and rebuild. Seven of their 13 rostered players are on rookie-scale or minimum deals.
Experts expect the Kings to be one of the worst teams in the league, near the bottom of the West. One preview predicts 26 or 27 wins, above the Vegas line of 21.5.
The Kings must stay out of the relegation zone this season.
Experts expect the Kings to keep pushing to win games instead of tanking.
Sabonis should play whenever he is available. Experts do not expect the Kings to bench him for Maxime Raynaud.
The team's direction is unclear and unstable, which lowers the fantasy value of Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis.
A Sabonis trade is possible. Sacramento might try to dump his contract at some point.
Zach LaVine has one year left on his contract.
LaVine could be traded, bought out or benched.
Russell Westbrook, DeMar DeRozan and Dennis Schroder are gone. They took shots and assists away from Sabonis and LaVine.
The ball is now concentrated with LaVine and Sabonis. Sabonis's usage should rise.
Of the players who took assists from Sabonis, LaVine and Huerter remain.
The departures should also free usage for Keegan Murray.
Kings passers had low assist conversion because teammates could not shoot. Westbrook is gone, but Nique Clifford, also named as a poor shooter, remains.
The projected starters are Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De'Andre Hunter, Keegan Murray and Domantas Sabonis.
Nobody is pushing the starting group for a spot.
The team seems to dislike Malik Monk, and experts do not trust his role. He is in the second unit.
There is no third point guard on the roster. Up to three roster spots are open.
Mike Miller is running the offense this season.
The Kings were the worst three-point team last season in both percentage and attempts.
Ham says this roster can shoot the three.
The Kings should be bad on defense. Poor backcourt defense could put frontcourt players in foul trouble and shift minutes to defenders who shoot threes.
Doug Christie is on a cheap contract and is under the most pressure. He may lean on veterans to win games.
Sacramento will give rookies minutes.
The Kings play 11 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, fourth most in the league, with only one back-to-back pair. Kings players who are still on rosters then get extra games.

tags.name: bottom team
tags.detail: Lowest Vegas win total (21.5). Experts see them near the bottom of the West.

tags.name: low shutdown risk
tags.detail: They must avoid the relegation zone, so they are expected to keep trying to win and to play Sabonis when he is available.

tags.name: trades likely
tags.detail: Sabonis could be traded or his contract dumped. LaVine could be traded or bought out.

tags.name: usage freed
tags.detail: Westbrook, DeRozan and Schroder are gone. Sabonis, LaVine and Murray gain shots and touches.

tags.name: concentrated usage
tags.detail: The ball runs through LaVine and Sabonis.

tags.name: good playoff schedule
tags.detail: 11 games in weeks 19 to 21 (rank 4 of 30), with one back-to-back pair.

note: Sabonis, LaVine and Keegan Murray gain the most because Westbrook, DeRozan and Schroder are gone. Relegation pressure means the Kings should keep trying to win rather than tank, and their 11-game fantasy playoff schedule is strong. Early on, watch for a Sabonis or LaVine trade or a LaVine buyout, which would reshape usage. Also watch whether Malik Monk, whom the team seems to dislike, stays stuck in the second unit.
